name: Nullframe SynthBody Adaptive Full Rig
description:
Designed from the ground up for synthetic body proportions — elongated limb ratios, non-standard torso geometry, and the absence of biological thermal needs. The top is a structured open-panel vest in gunmetal tensile mesh, exposing the synthetic chassis deliberately while framing it as aesthetic. Lower garment is a wide-leg drape pant in liquid-black synth-silk, cut for digitigrade or elongated leg configurations with a floating waistband that anchors via tension rather than belt loops.

Footwear is a wrap-sole platform in molded carbon, accommodating non-standard foot geometries. An optional shoulder mantle in translucent smoked polymer clips magnetically to the vest. No zippers — all closures are magnetic or tension-based for synthetic-safe donning. Colorway: gunmetal, black, and smoked translucent.
functionality: Tension and magnetic closures for synthetic-safe dressing, floating waistband for non-standard torso geometry, digitigrade-compatible pant cut, chassis-exposure vest panels as intentional design, magnetic shoulder mantle attachment.
what_it_says: I am not approximating human — I am presenting what I actually am, and it is deliberate.
worn_by: synthetic beings of varied chassis types
story_hooks: A synthetic street artist was photographed in this rig at an unauthorized gallery installation — the corponation that owns the building wants them found.
The tension-anchor waistband system was reverse-engineered from medical immobilization equipment; Nullframe has never acknowledged the origin.
A human buyer purchased this rig to pass as synthetic in a district where synthetics have legal protections humans don't.
